name: Attention Board
tag: One board that shows what needs your attention today across email, tasks and projects.

scenarios.title: Start the day
scenarios.ask: I have {emails} unread emails, {tasks} open tasks and {projects} projects. What needs me today?
steps: Scanned {emails} emails. {=round(emails * 0.08)} need a reply from you; the rest are updates or newsletters.
Found {=round(tasks * 0.15)} tasks due today or overdue.
Checked {projects} projects. {=max(1, round(projects / 4))} are waiting on your decision.
Ordered everything by deadline, who is waiting and impact.
followups: They stay in your inbox, grouped as updates and reading. Nothing is deleted or answered without you.
What if it's more than a day's work?
The board suggests what to push to tomorrow and drafts a short note for anyone who is waiting.

scenarios.title: Weekly review
scenarios.ask: Review my week: {done} tasks done, {slipped} slipped. What should change next week?
steps: Most slipped tasks were scheduled on days with over {=max(2, round(meetings / 5))} hours of meetings.
Suggested blocking {=max(2, 10 - round(meetings / 4))} hours of focus time next week.
Wrote a short review with 3 changes to try.
followups: No. It only suggests focus blocks. You decide what goes on the calendar.
The review is private by default. You can share a version without task details.

scenarios.title: Hand off before time off
scenarios.ask: I'm out for {days} days. Find what will need attention and who should cover it.
steps: Found {=days * 2} deadlines and meetings in the next {days}.
Matched each item to one of {team} teammates by who knows the work.
Drafted a handoff note for each person.
Drafted an out-of-office reply that points to the right person.
followups: What if no one knows a project?
The board marks it and suggests moving the deadline or a short briefing before you leave.
Does it catch me up when I'm back?
Yes. On your first day back it shows what happened and what still needs you.
